_comments: Adopts LAYERED base views for two core entities: CodeGen generates the full base view under
GeneratedBaseViewName, and the application owns BaseView, which wraps it as
These two are the first adopters in MJ core. 18 more entities still carry fully custom base
views (BaseViewGenerated = 0 with no inner name) and should follow over time — each one is
hand-maintaining generated SQL, and between them 25 foreign keys have no display field at all
because nobody went back to add the join.
MJ: Entities is deliberately NOT a candidate: vwEntities is what the metadata layer itself
reads, so layering the view CodeGen consults in order to decide whether to layer is a
Version Installations is the simplest possible case — no foreign keys at all, one computed
User View Run Details keeps two joins in its custom layer to surface UserViewID and EntityID,
which are two-hop ancestor keys rather than direct FK display fields — something CodeGen
cannot generate, and exactly the case layering exists for.
Layering also recovers the UserViewRun display field, which the hand-written view never had.
